revisions.note: Digital-assets research note (institutional-client only), via The Block’s coverage.
“Half-Year 2026” reframes the scenarios ($203B–$1.6T): the May base becomes the bull case. A {stat:drift_x}× cut, {stat:drift_weeks_words} weeks apart.
“Chainlink: Owning the rails” – lands within {stat:fork_gap_pct}% of 21Shares’ $350B by a completely different definitional route.
Binance Half-Year 2026 and SC “Owning the rails” folded into the chart, tables and matrix.
Grayscale’s ~$30B “today” figure and permissioned-rails lean added; every figure on this page now downloadable as data.json / data.csv / positions.csv.
“Breaking from the Pack” projects tokenized real-world assets growing from ~$40B to ~$2.3T by 2030. The desk’s May report, “Digital Rails, Real Economics”, had sized revenue only.
“Asset Tokenization 101” moves the desk from a stance to a forecast – tokenized real-world assets ex-stablecoins, $3T–$4T by 2035, labelled conservative.
The September “State of Tokenization” report (data to 30 Jun 2026) supersedes the Q1 edition; stablecoins are still counted in.

Standard Chartered’s $4T is now labelled as the 2028 figure it is (it sat on the 2030 chart unmarked); desk and forecast counts, the “same month” claim, the permissioned-layer multiple (was ten-fold, now ~{stat:permissioned_x}×) and the Binance cut interval ({stat:drift_weeks_words} weeks, was ten) corrected. Dataset restructured: one record per figure with horizon, as-of date and unit; stable desk ids; defined position vocabularies; JSON Schema and data dictionary.

revisions.change: First market size from the Fund: about $65B
revisions.note: The Global Financial Stability Report’s tokenization chapter sizes the public market for tokenized RWAs as of July 2026, leaving out repos, private tokenized markets and stablecoins.

Supply growth has stalled this year, the bank says, while usage keeps rising. The ~$4T-by-end-2028 call on this page counts stablecoins and has not been publicly restated. Client-only note, via The Block’s coverage.
IOSCO’s 2026 monitoring report, on RWA.xyz data: up from ~$16B on 1 Jul 2025. Its verdict: progressing, but transitional and fragmented.

revisions.change: Refresh to late November · source base 63 → 70 reports
revisions.note: Same-day readings from the RWA.xyz and DefiLlama dashboards (26 Nov) join the spring-vintage tracker numbers; DefiLlama’s $25.2B is superseded by its $30.8B reading. Seven reports published since August are folded in – Morgan Stanley × Oliver Wyman, Deutsche Bank, Pantera, The Block Research, the IMF, IOSCO and Standard Chartered’s October note. Citi’s bear–bull range added. Keyrock’s starting point corrected to $27B, the figure on its own page. The consensus numbers now carry a source and a date. Events the page described as upcoming – DTCC’s launch, the GENIUS rule-making, the CLARITY vote – rewritten as what happened.

chart_forecast.title: Market-size forecasts · 2030 horizon (SC: 2028)
chart_forecast.note_log: Log scale – marks are **dots, not bars**: on a log axis there is no zero, so length means nothing. Read position only.
chart_forecast.note_linear: Linear scale – the smallest forecast nearly vanishes. *That* {stat:fc_spread}× gap is the disagreement.

chart_today.note_log: Log scale – dots, not bars. {stat:td_desks_Words} desks, {stat:td_numbers_words} numbers, same market.
chart_today.note_linear: Linear scale – definitional choices swing today’s number ~{stat:td_spread}×. Colour is the definition.

chart_byscope.title: 2030 forecasts · grouped by scope
chart_byscope.note: Group the {stat:fc_n_words} forecasts by what they count and the {stat:fc_spread}× spread narrows: within a scope bucket the desks land ≤{stat:scope_max_spread}× apart. Definition explains most of the gap – not all of it.
